name: Run weekly hourly payroll
summary: Each week the payroll team turns the approved crew timecards of about 1,330 unionised carpenters, finishers, labourers and operators into pay by Thursday, under 15 to 20 collective agreements in several provinces. The ERP calculates pay, but specialists review the register by hand, fix errors, get a rule on agreement questions from labour relations, and have the run approved and released by two people. Source deductions go to the CRA within three working days of each weekly remitting period, and once a month the team reports hours and contributions to every union local and trust fund and pays WSIB. Errors cost money directly: late pay and late fund remittances carry penalties written into the agreements.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor with about 1,330 unionised hourly trades on weekly pay and about 10 payroll specialists for hourly and salaried payroll.
baseline.notes: One case is one weekly run, from the Tuesday timecard cut-off to the CRA remittance; the month's last run also carries union, trust fund and WSIB remittances.

trigger: The weekly timecard batches close at the Tuesday cut-off.
end_state: Workers are paid, the payroll is posted and source deductions remitted; after the month's last run, union, fund and WCB remittances are also paid and reconciled.

volume.seasonality: One run a week all year; the run is about 60% larger in summer than in winter as the field workforce moves between about 1,050 and 1,700.

evidence.note: Weekly pay is set by the ICI agreements (art. 22.02).

Bird posts weekly hourly payroll administrator roles; about 2 of the 10 payroll specialists on the hourly run itself (author's estimate), about 3 more on keying timecards (gc-spe-field-timekeeping) and the rest on salaried payroll and year-end.
Weekly approval and monthly remittance approval across regions.
Weekly release of the payment file.
Agreement questions and annual rate changes.
Handing out pay envelopes for about 135 crews each week.

systems.name: Construction ERP (job cost, general ledger, payables, receivables, payroll)
Government portals (WSIB clearance, Ministry of Labour notice of project, CRA, land registry)
Reporting and dashboards (Excel cost reports, Power BI)
Bank cash management portal (EFT and payment release)

steps.name: Run the missing-timecard report
steps.description: On Tuesday at the batch cut-off a payroll specialist runs the ERP report of active hourly employees with no hours this week for each region, and checks each name against layoffs, sick days and crews known to be rained out. Remaining gaps are chased with the general foremen.

error.defect_description: An active worker with no hours is assumed laid off and goes unpaid.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for about 1,330 hourly employees in three regions.

steps.name: Set up new hires and enter terminations
steps.description: The payroll specialist keys the week's new hires from the HR packets (TD1 forms, banking, union local, classification, benefit plan, province of work) into ERP payroll, and enters layoffs and terminations with final vacation pay so the records of employment can be issued.

error.defect_description: Wrong union local, classification or tax province gives the wrong rate, dues or deductions.

next.condition: no wage schedule change this week
a collective agreement wage or fringe increase takes effect

evidence.note: Bird's payroll administrator posting lists pay calculations for new hires, changes and terminations; about 30 hires and 25 terminations a week is the author's estimate from the organisation file volumes.

steps.name: Labour relations confirms the new wage schedule
steps.description: When an increase in a collective agreement takes effect (most ICI agreements move on 1 May), the labour relations manager reads the union's published wage and fringe schedule, confirms the effective date and how the increase is split between wages, vacation pay and funds, and tells payroll which rate tables change.

error.defect_description: Allocation between wage and funds misread.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; about 15 to 20 trade agreements across three provinces gives a few rate changes a year.

steps.name: Load the new rate tables in the ERP
steps.description: The payroll specialist updates the union rate tables for each affected local and classification: base rate, vacation and holiday pay percentage, dues check-off and each employer and employee fund contribution, then prints the table for the finance manager to compare with the schedule.

error.defect_description: A rate keyed wrong for one classification.

control.basis: Rate table changes independently checked before use

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: ERP calculates gross to net
steps.description: The ERP payroll calculation applies each worker's union rate, overtime and double time, shift premiums, travel and board allowances, vacation pay, income tax, CPP and EI, union dues check-off and the employer and employee fund contributions, and produces the payroll register.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Deductions and allowances follow the pay statement contents in art. 22.04 and contributions in art. 18.

steps.name: Review the payroll register for exceptions
steps.description: The payroll specialists work through the register region by region: negative or zero nets, more than 60 hours, overtime paid at straight time, board allowance outside the travel zone, missing fund contributions, and totals for hours and gross compared with last week by project. Each query is noted on an exceptions list.

error.defect_description: An error is missed and reaches a worker's pay.

control.basis: Internal control over payroll: register review before release

evidence.note: Author's estimate for a weekly union payroll of about 1,330 workers under many agreements.

steps.name: Correct errors and recalculate
steps.description: The payroll specialist fixes timecard lines, employee set-ups or rates, phones the general foreman when hours look wrong, and reruns the calculation for the affected workers before the register goes for approval.

error.defect_description: A correction creates a new error.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Labour relations rules on an agreement question
steps.description: The labour relations manager answers questions such as whether board allowance applies at a site outside the free travel zone, which shift premium applies, or which local's agreement covers a worker transferred between areas, and replies to payroll by email.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Travel zone, board allowance and shift premium rules (art. 17, 18.05-18.06, 20); time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Finance manager approves the payroll register
steps.description: The regional finance manager compares the register totals with last week and the head count, looks at large changes by project and the exceptions list, and approves the run in the ERP. The approver did not prepare the payroll.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Payroll preparer and approver are different people (internal control over financial reporting)

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Create the direct deposit file
steps.description: The payroll specialist generates the EFT file for workers paid by direct deposit and uploads it to the bank portal so funds arrive by 5 p.m. Thursday, and prints cheques with pay statements for workers still paid by cheque.

error.defect_description: Wrong file uploaded or bank details out of date.

control.basis: Collective agreement: direct deposit in the account by 5 p.m. Thursday (BACU-Guild ICI art. 22.03)

evidence.note: Art. 22.02-22.03 for pay day and method.

steps.name: Treasury releases the payment file
steps.description: The treasury manager checks the file total against the approved register and the bank balance, and releases the payment in the bank portal as the second authoriser.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Common treasury control; author's estimate.

steps.name: Courier pay envelopes to sites
steps.description: Cheques and pay statements in sealed envelopes go by courier or with a yard truck to each site trailer for Thursday, since the agreements require pay on the jobsite during working hours.

error.defect_description: Envelope sent to the wrong site.

evidence.note: Art. 22.02: pay on the jobsite by Thursday in a sealed envelope; transit time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Foremen hand out pay statements on site
steps.description: On Thursday each foreman hands his crew their envelopes or pay statements and collects any signed timesheet copies due. This is counted for all crews together.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: About 135 crews x 5 minutes; author's estimate.

steps.name: Direct deposits arrive on payday
steps.description: The bank credits the workers' accounts by 5 p.m. on Thursday from the file released on Tuesday or Wednesday; a rejected deposit comes back as an exception to payroll.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

steps.name: Answer pay queries and issue manual cheques
steps.description: On Thursday and Friday the payroll specialists take calls from workers and foremen about short or missing pay, check the timecard and register, and issue a manual cheque or direct deposit the next working day, because late pay carries a two-hour-a-day penalty in some agreements.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Collective agreement late pay penalty: two hours' pay per day after noon of the next working day (BACU-Guild ICI art. 22.05)

evidence.note: Art. 22.05; query volume is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Post the payroll journal and reconcile clearing accounts
steps.description: The payroll specialist posts the run to the general ledger and job cost with the labour burden (vacation pay, fund contributions, CPP, EI and WSIB), and reconciles the payroll clearing and deduction liability accounts.

error.defect_description: Burden posted to the wrong job or account.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Issue records of employment for laid-off workers
steps.description: For each worker laid off in the pay period the payroll specialist prepares the record of employment in ROE Web with insurable hours and earnings by pay period, so the worker can claim employment insurance.

error.defect_description: Insurable hours or last day paid wrong.

control.basis: Employment Insurance Regulations: record of employment for every interruption of earnings

evidence.note: Bird's posting lists ROE Web; about 25 layoffs a week x 5 minutes is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Remit source deductions to the CRA
steps.description: The payroll specialist totals income tax, CPP and EI (employee and employer) for the remitting period and pays the CRA through the bank by the third working day after the period ends, as a threshold 2 accelerated remitter.

error.defect_description: Late or short remittance attracts a penalty.

control.basis: Income Tax Act source deduction remittance: threshold 2 due 3 working days after each remitting period

next.condition: not the last run of the month

evidence.note: Weekly withholding of roughly $500,000 for 1,330 workers puts the company far above the $100,000 AMWA threshold.

steps.name: Prepare union and trust fund remittance reports
steps.description: After the month's last run the payroll specialists compile, for each local and agreement, every member's hours and earnings with dues check-off and each benefit, pension, training and industry fund contribution, fill in the union's remittance forms (three per month under some agreements) and prepare one cheque or EFT per payee.

error.defect_description: Hours reported to the wrong local or a fund omitted.

control.basis: Collective agreement remittance clause: contributions and dues with the report form by the 15th of the following month (BACU-Guild ICI art. 18.03-18.04)

evidence.note: Monthly remittance by the 15th with three forms per agreement; about 25 to 30 locals and agreements across three provinces is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Finance manager approves remittance payments
steps.description: The finance manager compares each remittance total with the payroll liability accounts and approves the cheques or EFTs before the due date, since remittances more than 10 days late attract liquidated damages.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Payment approval by someone other than the preparer

evidence.note: Art. 19.01: 5% a month on remittances more than 10 days in arrears.

steps.name: Report and pay workers' compensation premiums
steps.description: The payroll specialist reports the month's insurable earnings by rate group to the WSIB online and pays the premium, and files the equivalent reports for the Alberta, Saskatchewan, British Columbia and Atlantic boards on their own schedules.

error.defect_description: Earnings reported under the wrong rate group.

control.basis: Workplace Safety and Insurance Act: monthly premium reporting for insurable earnings of $1,000,000 or more

steps.name: Reconcile remittances to the general ledger
steps.description: The payroll specialist reconciles the month's dues, fund, CRA and WCB liability accounts to the remittances paid and clears differences, which feeds the month-end close.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Register errors
exceptions.description: Most weeks the register review finds timecard, set-up or rate errors that are fixed before approval.

exceptions.name: Agreement interpretation
exceptions.description: Board allowance, travel zone or premium question goes to labour relations.

exceptions.name: Wage schedule change
exceptions.description: A new wage and fringe schedule takes effect and rate tables are reloaded.

exceptions.name: Month-end remittances
exceptions.description: The month's last run also carries union, trust fund and WCB reporting and payment.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from timecard cut-off to the last remittance of the run
benchmarks.population: Weekly union payroll, Ontario ICI agreements

evidence.note: Pay by Thursday within four working days of closing the books (art. 22.02), CRA remittance 3 working days after the period; month-end runs wait for the 15th-of-month union deadline (art. 18.03).

pain_points.description: Many agreements, locals and provinces mean the register review and corrections take most of two working days every week.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Late or short pay draws calls from sites and manual cheques, and some agreements add two hours' pay per day of delay.
Monthly union remittance forms are compiled per local and fund by hand from payroll reports, and late remittances carry 5% a month in liquidated damages.

sources.title: When to remit (pay)
sources.supports: Accelerated threshold 2 remitters remit up to four times a month for the periods 1st-7th, 8th-14th, 15th-21st and 22nd-month end, each due by the 3rd working day after the period ends; a due date on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day.

sources.title: Types of remitters
sources.supports: Threshold 2 accelerated remitters are employers whose average monthly withholding amount two calendar years earlier was $100,000 or more; all payroll accounts of one organisation share the same remitter type.

sources.title: Policy in practice: Premium frequency
sources.supports: Businesses with annual insurable earnings of $1,000,000 or more report and pay WSIB premiums monthly and complete an annual reconciliation by 31 March.

sources.title: BACU-Guild Province Wide ICI Collective Agreement (marble, tile, terrazzo, cement masons, resilient floor layers and helpers), 1 April 2022 to 30 April 2025
sources.publisher: Brick and Allied Craft Union of Canada and Terrazzo, Tile & Marble Guild of Ontario; filed with Employment and Social Development Canada (Negotech)
sources.supports: Art. 5.01 employer hires from the Local Union office and the union supplies a referral slip; 5.02 recall within 35 days of layoff; 5.03 75% of additional hires may be requested by name; 5.05 hire from other sources as probationary members when the union cannot supply; 7.03 union refers only members with Fall Arrest, WHMIS and Working at Heights training; 18.03 deductions and contributions compiled monthly and remitted with the report form by the 15th of the following month; 18.04 three remittance forms each month; 19.01 5% a month liquidated damages on remittances more than 10 days in arrears; 22.01 timesheets mandatory, paper sheets due by end of business day Monday after the workweek; 22.02 time books closed weekly and Thursday payday within four working days of closing; 22.03 direct deposit by 5 p.m. Thursday; 22.04 pay statement contents; 22.05 two hours' pay per day of late pay; 24.01 normal week of four or five days of 8 to 10 hours.

sources.title: Payroll Administrator (Bird Construction job posting)
sources.supports: Bird Construction payroll administrator prepares and processes weekly and bi-weekly hourly payroll, calculates pay for new hires, changes and terminations, prepares Records of Employment in ROE Web, produces month-end reports and supports audits.

assumptions: The case starts at the Tuesday timecard cut-off; keying timecards is in gc-spe-field-timekeeping.

Hands-on time is for the whole run (all regions); the simulation adds it to elapsed time as if one person did it, which lengthens the simulated cycle by about two days compared with the specialists working in parallel.
About 80% of workers are paid by direct deposit and 20% by cheque on site in 2019-2022 (author's estimate).
The company is a threshold 2 accelerated remitter: weekly withholding of about $500,000 (1,330 workers x about $1,800 gross x about 25% tax, CPP and EI) is well over the $100,000 monthly threshold.

WSIB monthly reporting applies because Ontario insurable earnings are far above $1,000,000 a year; the WSIB page opened is the 2023 version of the threshold, which the company exceeds by a wide margin either way.
Remittances to the union locals are monthly, not weekly; the organisation file shows union_remittance as an output of this weekly process, which is true only of the month's last run (23% of runs).
Loaded costs come from the organisation file.
